mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the federal funds rate triggers a forward discounting effect, lowering the present value of future cash flows and producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in unemployment benefits (PAYEMS) exceeding 1,000 releases suppresses consumer confidence and corporate hiring intentions, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >1,000 in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods of high PAYEMS are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in unemployment benefits (PAYEMS) below 1,000 releases accelerates hiring and consumer spending, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in strengthening periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% signals weakening domestic demand, producing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >2% in a month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in contraction periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in retail sales (HOUST) exceeding 2% indicates excess demand relative to supply, compressing future discount rates and producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >2% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in periods of high HOUST are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in retail sales (HOUST) below 2% signals softening demand, producing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals a disinflationary trend, reducing expected future inflation and producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in disinflation periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
